subject: treasureChest
pitch: A pirate's treasure chest with its lid thrown open. Weathered dark wood planks bound with rusty iron straps and studs, a heavy padlock hanging loose, and spilling out of it: gold coins, a pearl necklace, a jewelled goblet and a few red and green gems. A small skull-and-crossbones is carved on the front.
reasoning:
I need to build a three.js module using the SDK's builder helpers, sticking only to the documented functions like createBuilder, joint, chain, sweep, and the various geometry/paint utilities available.

To keep things simple and avoid errors, I'll mostly rely on b.part with basic three.js geometries, and handle the hinged lid using a joint with a bone reference. Since it's unclear whether rotations should be baked into the geometry or handled via the `at`/`aim` options, I'll play it safe by rotating and translating the geometry directly with three.js methods before passing it into b.part, rather than relying on uncertain pose parameters.

Now I'm sketching out the full chest design: a box-plank body with subtle variation per plank, thin iron straps, spherical studs, a hinged lid rotated open at the back, a padlock made of a torus shackle and box body, scattered coin cylinders, a pearl necklace of small spheres, a lathe-generated goblet, low-poly gem shapes, and a simple skull-and-crossbones decoration on the front face using spheres and thin rotated boxes. I'm setting rough dimensions too — around 1 meter wide, 0.6 meters tall, and 0.5 meters deep for the main body.

I'm working out the hinge geometry for the open lid: it pivots at the back top edge, and I'm calculating the rotation math to figure out exactly where the lid center ends up when rotated about -110° on the X axis, confirming the lid swings up and backward as intended.

Rather than rotating geometry at render time, I'll bake the -110° rotation directly into the lid's box geometry before positioning it, then create a small helper function that builds a box, optionally pre-rotates it, and passes it to the part placement call with position and bone assignments.

I'm settling on a compact color palette — wood tones, iron and rust grays, gold, pearl, goblet bronze, and gem reds/greens — keeping the total under 64 colors. Now I'm figuring out how to assemble the body's front, back, and side panels out of individual vertical wood planks arranged across the width.

I'm planning the chest body as a hollow box: a dark interior floor set below the rim, surrounded by plank walls on front, back, and sides, with each wall built from a few evenly spaced plank segments of fixed width, height, and thickness. I'm now adding iron strap details — thin vertical bands across the front at a few x positions, plus horizontal bands to come.

For the lid, I'll construct it from plank boxes positioned relative to the hinge point, computing each plank's closed position via rotation offsets around the X-axis so they swing correctly when opened, matching the geometry's own rotation math so everything lines up consistently.

I'm trusting that bone rigging won't affect positioning since parts use model-space coordinates while joints only handle skeletal deformation — I'll add a "lid" joint at [0,0.6,-0.25] to anchor it. For the padlock, I'll hang it loosely from the front clasp with the shackle open, as described in the brief.

Working out the hasp and padlock placement on the body front — a hasp plate around (0.3,0.38,0.28), with the padlock's gold/iron body box dangling below it, and a torus shackle threaded through at roughly (0.3,0.33,0.30), rotated vertically and partially open. Now I'm thinking about where to place the skull and crossbones emblem on the front, trying to avoid overlapping the strap positions near x=0.

Positioning the skull as a bone-colored sphere with jaw and eye sockets at around (-0.05,0.3,0.285), with crossbones as two boxes crossed at ±40°, keeping everything just proud of the front planks' surface. Then I'm shifting to the treasure coins, planning them as flat gold cylinders randomly scattered and stacked inside the chest between y=0.5–0.62, with some spilling out over the front rim.

Adding scattered coins and a tilted pearl necklace...

Defining more lathe points...

I'm adding small octahedron gems scattered across the coin piles for detail, plus some spilled coins extending onto the floor in front of the chest for a natural overflow effect.

Now I'm working out the interior geometry: a dark wooden floor panel inset within the chest walls, with the front plank and side walls positioned to leave proper interior clearance, and figuring out the wall thickness and depth placement so everything aligns correctly.

Next I'm setting up the lid mechanics—hinge position at the back, closed-position offsets for the lid planks (five boards spanning the width), and adding iron cross-straps along the lid for detail. I'm also defining the rotation angle for opening the lid and how hinge position plus rotated offsets determine each plank's final placement.

Now I'm writing the helper function to build each box part, attach it to the correct bone, and apply rotation when needed, then starting the skeleton structure with a root joint before defining child joints for each component.

Adding small decorative geometry...

Good, the ring sits naturally in the hasp without rotation needed, just a slight tilt. Now I'm scattering a pile of 60 coins with randomized x and z positions within a shallow rectangular footprint.

Adding more coin placement details...

Base sits at 0.51 with roughly 0.17 height, so coins near x=0.2 may slightly overlap the goblet, which is acceptable. The chest rim is covered by the existing walls, so no extra work needed there, and now I'm sizing the skull as a sphere with radius 0.065.

Still working out skull geometry...

Now for the body planks, I'm using a wood color palette for subtle variation and laying out five planks across the front face, then planning side plank placement along similar spacing.

Still placing geometry...

Working out plank dimensions...

Still placing studs and straps...

I'm adding a padlock shackle as a torus overlapping the hasp body, positioning it so the ring partially sinks into the lock body for a realistic look, and noting the lid stays open so all this remains visible.

Now I'm starting the actual module code: setting up imports, exporting metadata for the treasure chest, defining a palette of wood, iron, rust, gold, pearl, and other colors, and adding a small seeded random number generator for variation.

I'm working out the hinge rotation math for the lid, applying a rotation matrix around the hinge point to compute offset positions, and writing a helper function to build lid boxes using this transform.

Now I'm planning out the plank and strap placements on the lid itself—sizing them, positioning them along x and z, and setting their heights relative to the plank tops so the straps sit correctly on top.

I'm also working out the coin pile inside the chest, randomizing each coin's x/z position within the interior bounds and scaling the vertical height based on distance from center, then starting to define the coin geometry as flat cylinders.

Writing coin geometry code...

Beyond that, I'm planning gold vs silver coin coloring, a spill of coins near the front opening, scattered gem positions on top of the pile, and a goblet shape built from a lathe profile placed near a bone chest prop, possibly with a gem accent.

Now I'm working out a pearl necklace spilling from the chest's front rim down to the floor, sagging along a curved path with coordinates easing from the rim toward the ground.

Next I'm shaping the skull: a scaled sphere flattened in z and slightly stretched in y, positioned near the top, with a small jaw box placed just below it.

Then I'm adding tiny black spheres for the eyes and a small black box for the nose. For the crossbones, I'm placing two long thin boxes rotated to form an X shape, and working out knob positions at the ends by computing offsets along each rotated bone's direction using cosine and sine of the rotation angle.

Adding corner brackets now, small iron boxes positioned at each corner of the plaque so they protrude slightly from the front face.

I'm adding a padlock using iron for the body and shackle, with a rust-colored hasp plate, then setting up the joint hierarchy connecting chest and lid with a parent relation, and writing a helper function to place parts with consistent color and bone assignment.

Writing box and sphere helpers...

Building the plank walls and floor...

Adding the iron straps around the front and back faces, positioning hinges and a padlock hasp...

Adding more iron straps to the sides and back mirroring the front pattern, then setting up the lid planks with their own strap reinforcements at offset positions.

Now I'm adding decorative studs on the lid as small spheres, plus scattering a few icosahedron gems colored red and green into a pile. For the coins, I'm generating a scattered pile using randomized positions within an elliptical footprint, varying height based on distance from center, and giving each coin cylinder slight random tilts for a natural scattered look.
